# Results

## Role dependence of player value measures

Role explained a large share of between-player variance in the box-score indices but almost none in RAPM (@tbl-eta, @fig-bias): η² was `{python} f2(V["eta2"]["PIR40"])` (95% CI `{python} ci(V["eta2_GA95"]["PIR40"])`) for PIR40 and `{python} f2(V["eta2"]["VAL40"])` (`{python} ci(V["eta2_GA95"]["VAL40"])`) for VAL40, compared with `{python} f2(V["eta2"]["RAPM"])` (`{python} ci(V["eta2_GA95"]["RAPM"])`) for RAPM. Rim protectors and interior bigs had the highest PIR40 and stretch forwards and wings the lowest, whereas in RAPM the differences between roles were small.

This pattern was not explained by the overlap between role variables and PIR components, by measurement error or by shrinkage. Among players with the same RAPM, role still explained a substantial share of the variance in PIR40 (partial η² = `{python} f2(V["RAPM_kosullu"]["PIR40"]["kismi_eta2"])`, 95% CI `{python} ci(V["RAPM_kosullu"]["PIR40"]["GA95"])`); at equal RAPM, interior bigs and rim protectors were rated `{python} f"{V['RAPM_kosullu']['PIR40']['rol_farki_RAPM_sabit']['2']:.1f}"` and `{python} f"{V['RAPM_kosullu']['PIR40']['rol_farki_RAPM_sabit']['4']:.1f}"` PIR points per 40 minutes higher than stretch forwards. With roles derived only from variables that are not PIR components, η² was `{python} f2(V["pir_bilesensiz_roller"]["eta2"]["PIR40"])` for PIR40 and `{python} f2(V["pir_bilesensiz_roller"]["eta2"]["RAPM"])` for RAPM. Split-half reliability was `{python} f2(V["guvenirlik"]["PIR40"]["spearman_brown"])` for PIR40 and `{python} f2(V["guvenirlik"]["RAPM"]["spearman_brown"])` for RAPM (n = `{python} V["guvenirlik"]["oyuncu_N"]` players), and reliability-corrected η² remained `{python} f2(V["eta2_duzeltilmis"]["RAPM"])` for RAPM, compared with `{python} f2(V["eta2_duzeltilmis"]["PIR40"])` for PIR40. A weaker RAPM penalty increased the spread of RAPM values (SD `{python} V["rapm_sd"]["ana"]` to `{python} V["rapm_sd"]["l1000"]` points per 100 possessions) without increasing η² (`{python} f2(V["eta2"]["RAPM_l1000"])`). PIR40 and RAPM were only weakly correlated (*r* = `{python} f2(V["korelasyon"]["RAPM"]["PIR40"])`).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-eta
#| tbl-cap: "Box-score indices differ between roles far more than RAPM does (mean value by main role and share of variance explained by role; players with at least 400 minutes)."
m = V["rol_ortalamasi_ham"]
rows = [{"Role": ROLE[k], "Players": V["rol_N"][k], "PIR40": f"{m[k]['PIR40']:.2f}", "VAL40": f"{m[k]['VAL40']:.2f}", "RAPM": f"{m[k]['RAPM']:.2f}"} for k in sorted(m, key=int)]
rows.append({"Role": "η² (95% CI)", "Players": V["oyuncu_N"],
             "PIR40": f"{V['eta2']['PIR40']:.2f} ({ci(V['eta2_GA95']['PIR40'])})",
             "VAL40": f"{V['eta2']['VAL40']:.2f} ({ci(V['eta2_GA95']['VAL40'])})",
             "RAPM": f"{V['eta2']['RAPM']:.2f} ({ci(V['eta2_GA95']['RAPM'])})"})
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

![Box-score indices, unlike RAPM, differ systematically between player roles. Bars show the mean of each value measure by main role, standardised across players (z-score), for players with at least 400 career minutes.](figures/fig1_role_bias.png){#fig-bias width=90%}

## Out-of-time predictive validity

In 2023–2024 segments, RAPM explained `{python} pp(T["RAPM"])`% of the possession-weighted variance in net rating, compared with `{python} pp(T["PIR40_toplami"])`% for summed PIR40 and `{python} pp(T["VAL40_toplami"])`% for summed VAL40. The advantage of RAPM was `{python} cipp(T["fark_GA95"]["RAPM-PIR40"])` percentage points over PIR40 and `{python} cipp(T["fark_GA95"]["RAPM-VAL40"])` percentage points over VAL40 (95% CIs from game bootstrap), so it was unlikely to be due to chance. Absolute values were small for all predictors, as expected for single lineup segments.

## Within-season validity of lineup value

Per standard deviation of within-team lineup value, second-half net rating changed by `{python} slope("RAPM")` points per 100 possessions for RAPM and `{python} slope("DAKIKA")` for first-half minutes, whereas the confidence intervals of all box-score measures included zero, whether computed from the first half (PIR40 `{python} slope("PIR40_sezon")`) or from all prior data (PIR40 `{python} slope("PIR40_havuz")`; VAL40 `{python} slope("VAL40_havuz")`) (@fig-slope). Box-score values could not be computed for low-minute players and covered `{python} f"{100 * I['kapsam']['PIR40_havuz']:.0f}"`% of segments with pooled data. In the common subset in which all measures were defined (`{python} f"{100 * I['ortak_alt_kume']['segment_payi']:.0f}"`% of segments), RAPM remained the only measure whose interval excluded zero (`{python} f"{I['ortak_alt_kume']['RAPM']['egim']:.2f}"`, 95% CI `{python} ci(I['ortak_alt_kume']['RAPM']['GA95'])`), but the paired differences between RAPM and pooled PIR40 (`{python} ci(I['ortak_alt_kume']['RAPM-PIR40_havuz']['GA95'])`) and minutes (`{python} ci(I['ortak_alt_kume']['RAPM-DAKIKA']['GA95'])`) were not statistically distinguishable from zero.

![Lineup value based on RAPM, unlike box-score indices, is associated with second-half net rating. Points: change in second-half net rating per standard deviation of within-team lineup value, adjusted for opponent RAPM and home advantage; bars: 95% team-season bootstrap confidence intervals.](figures/fig2_slopes.png){#fig-slope width=85%}

## Optimised lineups versus the coach's rotation

Second-half segments featuring at least four of the five players given most first-half minutes outperformed the team's other segments by `{python} contrast("DAKIKA_yok")` points per 100 possessions. Optimised fives shared on average about three of five players with this benchmark and were observed in a smaller share of possessions (@tbl-ilp). No optimisation variant differed from the coach benchmark under the same constraint: the paired differences ranged from `{python} f"{min(v['fark'] for v in CD.values()):.2f}"` to `{python} f"{max(v['fark'] for v in CD.values()):.2f}"` points per 100 possessions, and all confidence intervals included zero, spanning roughly ±4–5 points (@fig-ilp).

```{python}
#| label: tbl-ilp
#| tbl-cap: "Optimised fives share about three players with the coach's most-used five and do not outperform it (second-half net rating relative to the team's other lineups, paired difference from the coach benchmark under the same constraint, possession share, team-seasons and overlap with the coach five)."
SEL = {"DAKIKA": "Most-used players (coach)", "PIR40_sezon": "PIR40", "VAL40_sezon": "VAL40", "RAPM": "RAPM"}
RULE = {"yok": "none", "tez": "≥ 1 rim protector", "dengeli": "balanced"}
rows = []
for m_ in SEL:
    for r_ in RULE:
        k = f"{m_}_{r_}"
        rows.append({"Selection": SEL[m_], "Constraint": RULE[r_],
                     "vs team's other lineups": f"{C[k]['fark']:.2f} ({ci(C[k]['GA95'])})",
                     "vs coach benchmark": "—" if m_ == "DAKIKA" else f"{CD[k]['fark']:.2f} ({ci(CD[k]['GA95'])})",
                     "Possession share": f"{100 * C[k]['hucum_payi']:.1f}%", "Team-seasons": C[k]["takim_sezon"],
                     "Shared with coach five": "—" if m_ == "DAKIKA" else f"{OV[k]:.1f}"})
pd.DataFrame(rows).style.hide(axis="index")
```

![Optimised lineups perform no differently from the coach's most-used players. Points: difference in opponent-adjusted second-half net rating between segments featuring the optimised five and segments featuring the coach benchmark under the same constraint; bars: 95% team-season bootstrap confidence intervals.](figures/fig3_ilp.png){#fig-ilp width=85%}
